Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates an LLM’s ability to solve real-world software engineering issues by producing code patches that make a repository’s tests pass, using a curated set of tasks that have been verified as solvable. It stresses end-to-end debugging and code editing under realistic repo context, typically scored by whether the final patch passes the provided tests.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends the SWE-bench paradigm to multiple programming languages, requiring models to understand issue descriptions and modify codebases written in different languages and ecosystems. Performance depends on transferring debugging and patching skills across syntax, tooling, and library conventions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a more difficult and larger-scale software engineering benchmark designed to be more challenging and contamination-resistant, emphasizing realistic, multi-language, industrially relevant fixes. It tests whether models can reliably navigate complex repos, infer intended behavior, and implement robust patches.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic ability to complete real tasks inside a command-line environment, typically requiring iterative tool use (shell commands), inspection of files, and corrective actions. It stresses robust multi-step execution, error recovery, and maintaining task state across long interactions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp measures deep-research performance where models must answer difficult questions by searching and synthesizing information from a controlled web/document corpus. It emphasizes query planning, evidence integration across sources, and resisting unsupported answers when evidence is missing.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: τ2-bench evaluates an agent’s ability to resolve multi-turn customer-support tasks by interacting with simulated users and APIs while following domain policies (e.g., retail, airline, telecom). It stresses policy adherence, tool/API use, and dialogue-driven problem solving under constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Language Production (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control, Empathy (minor)

Description: OSWorld benchmarks multimodal computer-use agents performing tasks in an operating-system-like environment using screenshots and actions (e.g., clicking, typing). It tests whether the model can interpret GUI state, plan action sequences, and recover from mistakes across long horizons.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Sensorimotor Coordination (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid-intelligence benchmark where models infer latent rules from a few input-output grid examples and generate the correct output for a new grid. It is designed to emphasize novel pattern induction and compositional generalization with minimal task-specific priors.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Spatial Representation & Mapping, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon agent coherence by placing the model in a simulated year-long vending machine business scenario with many sequential decisions. The agent must manage inventory, pricing, negotiations, and strategy to maximize final balance under changing conditions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms, Episodic Memory (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas evaluates real-world tool use via Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, requiring models to discover tools, call them correctly, handle errors, and synthesize outputs. It emphasizes robust multi-step workflow execution across heterogeneous APIs and data sources.
Cognitive Functions:

L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates agentic performance on tasks resembling entry-level financial analyst work, often requiring retrieval, calculation, spreadsheet-like reasoning, and generating structured deliverables. L1:
